skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Students recognize key concepts about financial intermediaries and their roles.

Students understand basic differences between monetary and financial issues, quantity theory of money demand, Keynes's theory of money demand, modern quantity theory of money demand by M. Friedman, empirical evidence on money demand.
Students analyze central bank operations, including money supply processes and monetary policy tools.
Students evaluate causes and effects of inflation, including prevention measures.
Students gain fundamental knowledge about international finance, including foreign exchange markets and balance of payments.
Students develop analytical problem-solving skills to address practical issues within the scope of monetary and financial theories.
Students acquire independent work skills, dynamic and diverse teamwork skills, and presentation skills.
